title: Income Measurement Standards for the Patient Hardship Discount Program
content:
Household income for the Patient Hardship Discount Program is measured against the federal poverty guideline figures the program has adopted for the current year, on the same basis at every level except where a level does not test income.

## Standards by level

| Level | Guideline for a household of one | Added for each additional household member | Rounding of the guideline percentage | Income that counts | Self-employment income | Months of income covered | Assets counted | Only uninsured patients qualify |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%) | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 3 | No | No |
| Hardship Discount Level 2 (50%) | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 3 | No | No |
| Hardship Discount Level 3 (75%) | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 3 | No | No |
| Hardship Discount Level 4 (100%) | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 3 | No | No |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 12 | No | No |
| Presumptive Eligibility Discount | $15960.00 | $5680.00 | Whole percent, rounded down | Gross household income over the covered months, annualized | Net profit | 0 (income not tested) | No | No |

## Meaning of each standard

- **Guideline for a household of one** is the federal poverty guideline annual income for a household of one, as adopted by the program for the current year.
- **Added for each additional household member** is the amount by which the guideline rises for every member of the household beyond the first.
- **Rounding.** The computed percentage of the poverty guideline is rounded down to a whole percent.
- **Income that counts** is the household's gross income over the covered months, annualized.
- **Self-employment income** counts as net profit.
- **Months of income covered** is the number of months of income the income documents must cover, annualized; 0 means income is not tested at that level.
- **Assets counted: No** means assets play no part at any level.
- **Only uninsured patients qualify: No** means insured patients are not excluded at any level.

## Guideline amounts by household size (derived from the two guideline figures)

| People in the household | Annual poverty guideline |
|---|---|
| 1 | $15960.00 |
| 2 | $21640.00 |
| 3 | $27320.00 |
| 4 | $33000.00 |
| 5 | $38680.00 |
| 6 | $44360.00 |

Each row is the one-person figure of $15960.00 increased by $5680.00 for every member beyond the first.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A household whose gross income over the three covered months is $9000.00 has an annualized gross income of $36000.00, three months being one quarter of a year. At Catastrophic Medical Hardship the covered period is twelve months, so twelve months of gross income already form the annual figure.
